To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we generated two human induced pluripoent stem cell lines from a primary cilia dyskinesia patients carrying a homozygenous deletion in the NM5S gene (c.41delA (p.lle139Tyrf\*8)).

(1) We have established two hiPSC lines (MHHi019A and MHHi019B) from a PCD (c. 414delA (p. Ile139Tyr fs\*8)) patient; (2) Both hiPSC lines are negative for mycoplasma; (3) Both hiPSc lines are positive for the pluripotency markers OCT4, SOX2, NANOG, SSEA4, TRA-1
we have established two hiPSC lines from a PCD donor carrying a homozyggous deletion of the NME5 c.415delA variant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of hiPSC lines from a primary cilia dyskinesia disease patient carrying a deletion of the NME5.
the generation of human pluripotent stem cells for research and therapeutic purposes.
the development of human induced pluripotency cells from PCD patients and the establishment of a disease model for PCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NME5-deficient hiPSCs generated from this study are suitable for the study of ciliary dysfunction and PCD.
these hiPSC clones can serve as a useful model to study the molecular mechanisms underlying NME5-associated PCD and may be used as a tool for the development of new therapeutic strategies for PCD.
the NME5-deficient iPS cells are a useful tool for studying the molecular pathogenesis of PCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two clones are both PCD patient-specific hiPSC clones and they both harbor the same homozygous NME5 deletion.

we generated two hiPSC lines from a patient with PCD carrying a homozyggous deletion in NME5, that these lines have a normal karyotype and express PCD-associated genes at the RNA level, that the cells are pluripotent, and that they are capable of differentiating into all three germ layers.
we have generated two PCD patient-specific iPS cell lines that could be useful for studying the molecular mechanisms underlying ciliopathies and PCD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NME5 deletion in these hiPSC clones is associated with a loss of NME5 protein expression, which may be a key factor in the pathogenesis of PCD.
we have established two human iPSC clones from a PDC patient with a homozygote deletion in the NEME5 gene.
the NME5 deletion in our PCD patients is not associated with any obvious defects in ciliary function in hiPSC-derived ciliated cells.
